source.title: Mechanistic Interpretability for End-to-End Self-Driving
source.authors: Manav Gagvani; Benjamin Namikas; Sivamurugan Velmurugan; N. Kumar; Shreyyash Sharma; Thomas Peterson; Pratyush Mathur; Hyunseo Chang; R. Paleja

page_placements.theme: Downstream utility depends on task and comparison baseline

record.tranche_reason: The study applies SAE-based feature analysis in a new setting, an end-to-end driving planner, and reports results on the features it recovers. It does not test superposition geometry or the original toy-model mechanism.
record.gate_note: The paper cites superposition as motivation but does not vary feature sparsity or importance, test whether excess features are dropped or overlap, or measure feature-direction geometry. Rows below concern the study's own SAE feature recovery, visual grounding, steering, and representation-utility results. The cited claims about other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The paper cites superposition only as motivation and uses TopK SAEs as a tool on a monocular driving planner. It reports how interpretable, grounded, steerable and useful its own SAE latents are. It does not test superposition or any version. No version varies sparsity or capacity or measures feature geometry, and none compares SAE features with neuron polysemanticity. The SAE is not overcomplete (384 latents on a 384-d query), so it cannot show more features than dimensions. The subject is a driving transformer, not an LLM. Under the same-system rule, its SAE findings do not bear on V4, and V5 and V6 are not examined.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that SAE latents in their single-camera planner are structured, visually grounded and steerable, recovering route intent at 98.3% unsupervised. They also conclude that an SAE-latent scorer adapter cuts ADE@5s by 3.44%, beating dense-query and random-init encoder controls. They note that evaluation is open-loop, single-camera, and dependent on edit quality, and that edit and steering alignment is moderate. They make no claim about superposition itself.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains TopK SAEs with AuxK loss on an end-to-end driving planner's query activations; it does not reproduce the toy-network setup or measure superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The cluster structure varies with co-activation threshold: τ = 0.20 merges many features, while τ = 0.35 and τ = 0.40 retain the principal intent-aligned structure with different memberships.

fits_no_version.finding: In a 384-d driving-planner query, a non-overcomplete TopK SAE yields latents. Co-activation clusters of these latents align with route intent and speed (98.3% intent recovery), and the latents are visually grounded (image main effect 14.3% of variance).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents on non-language E2E driving policies form interpretable, input-grounded feature groups.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering SAE latents changes planner outputs, but visual-edit and steering alignment is moderate (61% sign match, r = 0.172). Natural-association versus steering sign match is 40–62% across statistics (Table 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Visually responsive SAE latents in driving planners only moderately predict their causal steering effects.

fits_no_version.finding: An adapter on SAE latents beats dense-query (2.74%) and random-init encoder (2.86%) controls in ADE reduction (3.44%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse SAE latents are a more useful input for post-hoc scorer correction than dense activations.

record.problems: The study uses one planner architecture and a single-camera setup; it does not test closed-loop behavior. The authors say counterfactual edits may be imperfect or confounded by the detector and image editor, and acknowledge that visual-edit/steering alignment is moderate. Most feature-steering results lack uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, no sparsity variation, no overlap geometry or phase transition.
All: no capacity pressure, importance, or dedicated-versus-shared dimensions.
All: no analysis of neuron polysemanticity or its causes.
Not tested in LLMs. No neuron-level distribution analysis. The SAE is not overcomplete, so recovery of more features than dimensions is not tested.
No test of completeness, canonicality, or stability across seeds or checkpoints. There is a single SAE with seed 42.
No test of feature dimensionality. Steering acts on scalar nonnegative latents only.

missing.what: Feature activity statistics: 125 of 384 block-3 latents fire on <0.5% of scenes, and only 340 activate at all on validation. Steering sweep: 254 of 340 have control score >0.01 and 68 have >0.1. Also the natural-versus-steering agreement table. These are relevant to the fits_no_version steering finding.
missing.locator: Appendix C.1; Appendix F.4; Table 7; Table 8

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3, supports V4' is overturned. V4 concerns LLMs, and this is a driving transformer. The SAE has as many latents as the activation dimensions, so it cannot evidence superposition. The intent clusters partly reflect an intent input injected directly into the query. The paper cites Toy Models only as motivation for using SAEs.

versions.untested_parts: No test of toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometric structure.
No test of capacity pressure, feature importance, or dedicated versus shared neuron dimensions.
No test of whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
The study tests SAE-recoverable features in one E2E driving planner, not LLMs; it does not establish that features are spread across many neurons or test the more-features-than-dimensions condition.
No test that SAE features are complete, canonical units or stable across model checkpoints or SAE training runs. Clustering robustness across settings does not establish those properties.
The study steers scalar SAE latents but does not test whether the underlying model features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: SMTS
rows.size_stated: Decoder hidden dimension 384; SAE latent dimension 384
rows.stage_stated: Planner trained on 250,000 WOD-E2E samples for 10 epochs; SAEs trained on activations from the complete training split
rows.operation_detail: Clustered block-3 SAE latents using binarized co-activation correlations at threshold τ = 0.35
rows.value: Four clusters: C0, 64 latents, Straight; C1, 36, Left; C2, 34, Straight; C3, 27, Right
rows.note: The paper describes the clusters as organized around route intent and vehicle motion.
rows.check: Co-activation clusters of SAE latents in a driving planner, not an LLM. Route intent is an explicit one-hot input injected into the query, so intent-aligned clusters say nothing about superposition. The SAE is not overcomplete (384→384).

rows.subject: SMTS
rows.size_stated: Decoder hidden dimension 384; SAE latent dimension 384
rows.stage_stated: Planner trained on 250,000 WOD-E2E samples for 10 epochs; SAEs trained on activations from the complete training split
rows.operation_detail: Assigned scenes to clusters by highest mean activation and mapped clusters to route intent by majority vote
rows.value: 98.3% overall; 99.8% straight, 92.9% left turns, and 86.4% right turns
rows.note: The route-intent label was assigned from the cluster activation; the paper describes the recovery as unsupervised.
rows.check: Clusters are mapped to intents by majority vote on the same validation data. Intent is a direct model input. This is not evidence on any version.

relation.reason: Superposition motivates the SAE approach; the experiments evaluate the resulting representations and driving method rather than superposition itself.

tranche.reason: Uses SAEs to analyze and improve a driving planner; reports feature interpretability, steering and adapter utility without testing any listed claim version.

source_check.notes: Rows r13–r15 report method utility and correctly remain unlinked to claim versions with state cannot_determine. Reductions are relative ADE@5s improvements from reranking fixed proposals in a single-camera, open-loop evaluation.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SMTS on WOD-E2E, for the tested SAE analyses
reader_labels.reason: The learned latents formed route- and speed-aligned clusters, depended on visual inputs, and showed visual-edit and steering responses; see r1–r3, r7–r12.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Cluster structure became too coarse at τ = 0.20, membership changed at τ = 0.40, and visual-edit/steering agreement was moderate; see r4, r5, r12.
